birthsYearEndingMar2026.evidenceQuote: In the year ending 31 March 2026: there were 292,500 births ... births increased by 1,000 (0.3%) since the previous year

deathsYearEndingMar2026.evidenceQuote: In the year ending 31 March 2026: there were 191,900 deaths ... deaths increased by 5,800 (3.1%) since the previous year

migrationDeparturesYearEndingMar2026.evidenceQuote: In the year ending 31 March 2026: there were 265,400 people emigrating from Australia ... departures decreased by 6,100 people (2.2%) since the previous year

revisionCaveat.evidenceQuote: All data after 30 June 2021 are subject to revision.

birthsRegistered2024.evidenceQuote: There were 292,318 registered births in 2024, an increase of 1.9% (or 5,320 births) from 2023.

totalFertilityRate2024.evidenceQuote: The total fertility rate was 1.481 births per woman .

tfrTrend.value: 1.481 in 2024 vs 1.499 in 2023 and 1.795 in 2014; below replacement since 1976
tfrTrend.evidenceQuote: Australia's total fertility rate: was 1.481 babies per woman in 2024, lower than 2023 (1.499) and the rate 10 years ago (1.795 in 2014); has been below replacement since 1976.

replacementLevel.evidenceQuote: The total fertility rate required for replacement is considered to be around 2.1 babies per woman to replace herself and her partner in the absence of overseas migration.

medianAgeOfParents.evidenceQuote: Median age was 32.1 years for mothers and 33.9 years for fathers.

sexRatioAndMarriage.value: 105.8 male births per 100 female births; 60.8% of births to parents in a registered marriage

deathsRegistered2025.evidenceQuote: There were 188,421 deaths registered in 2025, an increase of 1,153 from 2024 (187,268).

standardisedDeathRate.evidenceQuote: The standardised death rate decreased to 4.955 deaths from 5.078 in 2024.

infantDeaths.value: 1,019 (up 62); infant mortality rate 3.40 per 1,000 live births
infantDeaths.evidenceQuote: Infant deaths increased by 62 deaths to 1,019.

malesAtBirth.evidenceQuote: Life expectancy at birth was 81.1 years for males and 85.1 years for females in 2022 – 2024, reflecting no change for either males or females from the previous year (2021 – 2023).

femalesAtBirth.evidenceQuote: Life expectancy at birth was 81.1 years for males and 85.1 years for females in 2022 – 2024, reflecting no change for either males or females from the previous year (2021 – 2023).

highestLowestByState.value: Highest ACT (males 82.0, females 85.8); lowest NT (males 77.0, females 80.7)
highestLowestByState.evidenceQuote: Life expectancy was highest in the Australian Capital Territory for both males (82.0 years) and females (85.8 years). ... Life expectancy was lowest in the Northern Territory for both males (77.0 years) and females (80.7 years).

trendCommentary.value: Unchanged from 2021-2023; 2020-2022 and 2021-2023 decreases were the first since the mid-1990s; +0.8 years (males) and +0.7 years (females) over the past decade; male-female gap 4.0 years
trendCommentary.evidenceQuote: Life expectancy was unchanged from 2021 – 2023, following decreases in that period and the previous period (2020 – 2022), which were the first decreases since the mid-1990s. ... erp.releaseTitle: Estimates of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians, 30 June 2021

erpAt30June2021.value: 983,700 people (3.8% of the total Australian population)
erpAt30June2021.evidenceQuote: At 30 June 2021, there were 983,700 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, representing 3.8% of the total Australian population:

under15.evidenceQuote: One-third (33.1%) were under 15 years of age.

aged65Plus.evidenceQuote: People aged 65 years and over comprised 5.4% of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander population compared with 17.2% of the non-Indigenous population.

distribution.value: 74.5% lived in NSW, Queensland and WA combined; NT highest proportion (30.8%), Victoria lowest (1.2%)
distribution.evidenceQuote: Three-quarters (74.5%) lived in New South Wales, Queensland and Western Australia combined. ... The Northern Territory had the highest proportion of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people relative to its total population size (30.8%), and Victoria had the lowest (1.2%).

identificationCategories.evidenceQuote: Among the 983,700 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people in 2021: 91.7% identified as Aboriginal; 4.0% identified as Torres Strait Islander; 4.3% identified as both Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander.

contextualWording.evidenceQuote: The increase in the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander population is not wholly explained by demographic factors. The change in Census counts between 2016 and 2021 is explained in Understanding change in counts of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians: Census.

censusCount.releaseTitle: Census of Population and Housing - Counts of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians, 2021

census2021Count.value: 812,728 people (3.2% of total population), up from 649,171 (2.8%) in 2016, a 25.2% increase
census2021Count.evidenceQuote: 812,728 people identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in 2021 – up from 649,171 in 2016 ... Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people represented 3.2% of the total population – up from 2.8% in 2016

historicalFraming.evidenceQuote: The 2021 Census marks 50 years since the 1971 Census – the first Census to include all Australians following the 1967 Referendum. ... In 1971, 115,953 people identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census. In 2021, that number grew to 812,728 people.

identificationCategories.evidenceQuote: Of the 812,728 people who identified as being of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin in 2021: 91.4% identified as Aboriginal; 4.2% identified as Torres Strait Islander; 4.4% identified as Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander.

wherePeopleLived.evidenceQuote: Just over one-third (34.2%) of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people lived in New South Wales in 2021. A further 29.2% lived in Queensland and 10.9% lived in Western Australia.

totalHouseholds.evidenceQuote: The number of households is projected to increase from 10.0 million in 2021 to between 13.3 and 13.9 million in 2046.

householdsByType2021.value: Family households 6,950.7 thousand; Group households 405.7 thousand; Lone person households 2,637.5 thousand; Total 9,993.9 thousand
householdsByType2021.evidenceQuote: Family households 6,950.7 ... Group households 405.7 ... Lone person households 2,637.5 ... Total households 9,993.9

householdTypeShares2046.value: Family households 68%-70%; lone person 26%-28%; group 4%-5% of all households in 2046
householdTypeShares2046.evidenceQuote: Family households are projected to remain the most common household type in Australia, at 68% to 70% of all household in 2046. ... Lone person households are projected to make up 26% to 28% of all Australian households in 2046. ... Group households are projected to make up 4% to 5% of all households in 2046.

averageHouseholdSize.value: 2.6 people per household in 2021; projected 2.4-2.6 in 2046; 2.57 in 2021 (international comparison), projected 2.55 in 2031
averageHouseholdSize.evidenceQuote: In 2046 there are projected to be between 2.4 and 2.6 people per household on average. This is similar to the 2021 average of 2.6. ... The average household size for Australia was similar to New Zealand in 2021 (2.57 and 2.70 respectively), but this is projected to decrease in Australia (2.55 in 2031).

families.value: 7.2 million families in 2021, projected to 9.5-9.7 million in 2046; couples with children 44% of families in 2021 (3,117.6 thousand); couples without children 39% (2,763.7 thousand); female lone parent families 13% in 2021; one parent families 1,150.1 thousand
families.evidenceQuote: The number of families is projected to increase from 7.2 million to between 9.5 and 9.7 million. ... Couples with children are projected to make up 42% to 43% of all families in 2046; down slightly from 44% in 2021. ... Couples without children are projected to be the second most common family type, at 38% to 40% in 2046 (39% in 2021). ... Female lone parent families are projected to make up 13% to 14% of all families in 2046 (compared to 13% in 2021).

livingArrangements2021.value: 48% of Australians lived in a couple family with children; one-parent families ~12% of population (2001-2021); 10% living alone; 20% of lone parents were male
livingArrangements2021.evidenceQuote: 48% of Australians lived in a couple family with children. ... The proportion of people living in one parent families remained around 12% between 2001 and 2021. ... The proportion of people living alone increased from 9% in 2001 to 10% in 2021. ... In 2021 one in five (20%) lone parents were male (17% in 2001).

caveat.evidenceQuote: Projections are not predictions or forecasts. They are an illustration of what would happen if certain assumptions about the future living arrangements of Australia's population were to persist over the projection period.

nomDefinition.sourceTitle: Measuring Net Overseas Migration in Australia (ABS article, 12/12/2024)

definition.evidenceQuote: Net overseas migration (NOM) is a demographic concept which reflects the number of people added to (or subtracted from) the Australian population due to international migration.

twelveSixteenMonthRule.evidenceQuote: Finalised NOM estimates are determined based on whether a traveller has spent 12 of the last 16 months in or out of Australia. This is known as the 12/16 month rule. ... A person who is not already resident in Australia, is added to the estimated resident population (ERP) if they travel to Australia and remain present in Australia for 12 months or more (an overseas migrant arrival). Likewise, an Australian resident is removed from the population if they leave Australia for 12 months or more (an overseas migrant departure). ... The 12 months does not have to be continuous and is measured over a 16-month period.

revisionProcess.evidenceQuote: Preliminary NOM is revised each quarter for four quarters. As more time elapses, each revision can use more information about travellers' lengths of stay in or out of Australia as it becomes known. After the fourth revision, NOM is regarded as final as it is based on actual migration outcomes, and will then reflect any changes in travel behaviour which have occurred.

erpVsCensusDistinction.sourceTitle: National, state and territory population methodology, March 2026

erpScope.evidenceQuote: Australia's estimated resident population (ERP) includes all people who usually live in Australia (regardless of nationality, citizenship or visa status), with the exception of people present for foreign consular or diplomatic reasons.

censusBasis.evidenceQuote: The latest ERP is based on adjusted 2021 Census counts, updated with quarterly estimates of births, deaths, overseas and interstate migration. ... The 30 June ERP in a Census year is calculated by: adjusting Census counts of Australian usual residents to account for people missed or counted twice in the Census (based on Post Enumeration Survey results) ... adding usual residents temporarily overseas on Census night; adjusting for births, deaths and migration from 30 June to Census night.

medianAge.evidenceQuote: The median age for Australia is projected to increase from 38.5 years in 2022 to between 43.8 and 47.6 years in 2071.

ageingNarrative.evidenceQuote: Of the changes projected to occur in Australia's population, ageing is generally considered to be the most dramatic, with significant changes to the age structure of the population. Ageing of the population is a trend which has been evident over recent decades as a result of fertility remaining below replacement level and declining mortality rates. In all series this trend is projected to continue.

ageStructure.evidenceQuote: The proportion of: children aged 0-14 years is projected to decline from 18% in 2022 to between 13% and 16% in 2071; the working age population aged 15-64 years is projected to decrease from 65% to between 59% and 60% in 2071; people aged 65 years and over will increase from 17% in 2022 to between 25% and 27% in 2071; people aged 85 years and over will increase from 2.1% in 2022 to between 5.2% and 6.4% in 2071
